results.title: Highly composite numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A positive natural number is highly composite if it has strictly more divisors than every smaller positive natural number.

results.title: Exponents of highly composite numbers are non-increasing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $H$ is a highly composite number and $p \le q$ are primes, then the exponent of $q$ in the prime factorization of $H$ is at most the exponent of $p$.

results.title: Prime divisors of highly composite numbers form an initial segment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $H$ is a highly composite number and $p \le q$ are primes with $q \mid H$, then $p \mid H$. In other words, the set of primes dividing $H$ is an initial segment of the primes.
